name: Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Ruins of Songo Mnara
description: On two small islands off Tanzania's southern coast lie the stone ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Songo Mnara, once thriving Swahili trading ports. From the 13th to the 16th century, their merchants handled gold, pearls, perfumes and Chinese porcelain, placing them at the heart of Indian Ocean commerce. At its height, Kilwa had over 10,000 inhabitants, and its ruins still draw visitors by boat.
